The test `test_setitem_ndarray_3d` checks whether the `setitem` operation on an IntervalTree object is correctly raising a ValueError when trying to set values with an ndim greater than 1. However, the test failure indicates that this is not the case.

Following the execution path, we find that the IntervalTree class does not have a method to check for the number of dimensions of the input array `nd3`. The method `get_loc` in IntervalTree is responsible for setting values at specific intervals, but it does not perform any checks on the shape of the input array.

Consequently, when trying to set values with an ndim greater than 1 (in this case, a 3D numpy array), the error occurs because the method `get_loc` in IntervalTree is being called without checking whether the input array has more dimensions than expected. 

The error message "Buffer has wrong number of dimensions (expected 1, got 3)" suggests that the IntervalTree class expects the input to be a 1D array, but a 3D numpy array was provided instead.

Standard libraries like numpy and pandas have various checks to ensure that data is correctly dimensioned before performing operations on it. However, in this case, the IntervalTree class does not seem to perform these checks, leading to an incorrect error message being raised when trying to set values with a 3D numpy array.
